result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Poisson]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Poisson family with log (canonical) link. twitter-card: title: >- [Poisson]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} | whittaker description: Poisson family with log (canonical) link. title: "[Poisson]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Poisson family with log (canonical) link. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Poisson family with log (canonical) link. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L13-L269){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-class} ```pythonsignature Poisson() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Poisson family models the response as non-negative integer counts, such as the number of events observed in a fixed interval of time, space, or exposure. It is the standard choice for count data when the variance of the counts is approximately equal to their mean. The canonical log link guarantees positive fitted values on the response scale and gives the linear predictor a multiplicative interpretation: a one-unit increase in a covariate multiplies the expected count by `exp(coefficient)`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The canonical link is the natural logarithm: $$ g(\mu) = \log(\mu) $$ The variance function is $V(\mu) = \mu$, so the variance equals the mean. If the observed variance substantially exceeds the mean (overdispersion), consider `NegativeBinomial` or `Tweedie` instead. The deviance is $$ D(y, \hat\mu) = 2 \sum_i \left[ y_i \log\!\left(\frac{y_i}{\hat\mu_i}\right) - (y_i - \hat\mu_i) \right] . $$ ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAM to simulated count data with a smooth, log-linear trend: ::: {#f37930c0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 200 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = np.exp(0.5 * np.sin(x)) y = rng.poisson(mu) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.Poisson()) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Poisson(link='log') Inference: REML Observations: 200 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err z value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.2113 0.0657 3.214 0.00131 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 4.18 5 37.260 5.312e-07 Total EDF: 5.18 Scale est: 1.000000 Deviance: 187.0851 Null dev: 230.5815 Dev. expl: 18.9% GCV score: 0.985797 AIC: 554.30 BIC: 571.37 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [scale_known](#scale_known){.doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Whether the dispersion parameter is fixed. Always `True` for Poisson. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [scale_known]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Whether the dispersion parameter is fixed. Always `True` for Poisson. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [scale_known]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Poisson distribution has no free dispersion parameter, so the scale is fixed at `1` and is never estimated during fitting. This affects how `GAM.summary()` reports the scale and how many degrees of freedom are attributed to dispersion estimation. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods} | Name | Description | |---|---| | [deviance()](#deviance){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Total Poisson deviance, the (weighted) sum of `unit_deviance`. | | [initialize()](#initialize){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Starting values for `mu`: `y` nudged away from zero. | | [link()](#link){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Apply the log link: $\eta = \log(\mu)$. | | [link_derivative()](#link_derivative){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Derivative of the log link: $g'(\mu) = 1/\mu$. | | [link_inverse()](#link_inverse){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Apply the inverse log link: $\mu = e^{\eta}$. | | [log_likelihood()](#log_likelihood){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Poisson log-likelihood $\ell_i = y_i \log(\mu_i) - \mu_i - \log(y_i!)$. | | [simulate()](#simulate){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Simulate Poisson-distributed response values with mean `mu`. | | [unit_deviance()](#unit_deviance){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Per-observation Poisson deviance contributions. | | [variance()](#variance){.doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Poisson variance function: $V(\mu) = \mu$. | : {.gd-summary-table} ### [deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Total Poisson deviance, the (weighted) sum of `unit_deviance`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L129-L149){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature deviance( y, mu, *, weights=None, ) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values (counts), shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional prior weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total (weighted) deviance. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Starting values for `mu`: `y` nudged away from zero. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L250-L266){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Since the log link requires strictly positive `mu`, small or zero counts are pushed away from zero to avoid `log(0)` on the first P-IRLS iteration. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values (counts), shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting values for `mu`, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the log link: $\eta = \log(\mu)$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L62-L76){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link(mu) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. Should be positive; values are clipped to `_EPS` to avoid `log(0)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values $\eta = \log(\mu)$, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Derivative of the log link: $g'(\mu) = 1/\mu$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L96-L109){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link_derivative(mu) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Derivative values $1/\mu$, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Apply the inverse log link: $\mu = e^{\eta}$. ::: ::: ```pythonsignature link_inverse(eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The linear predictor is clipped to `[-30, 30]` before exponentiating to guard against overflow while fitting. ::: #### Parameters [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L178-L208){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Ignored. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional prior weights, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The total log-likelihood. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate Poisson-distributed response values with mean `mu`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L231-L248){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature simulate( mu, scale, rng, ) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mean (fitted values), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Ignored (the Poisson distribution has no free dispersion parameter). [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [np.random.Generator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `numpy.random.Generator` instance. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated response values, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [unit_deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Per-observation Poisson deviance contributions. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L151-L176){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature unit_deviance( y, mu, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes $d_i = 2 \left[ y_i \log(y_i / \hat\mu_i) - (y_i - \hat\mu_i) \right]$, with the convention $y_i \log(y_i / \hat\mu_i) = 0$ when $y_i = 0$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed response values (counts), shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Per-observation deviance contributions, shape `(n,)`. ::: ### [variance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Poisson variance function: $V(\mu) = \mu$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/poisson.py#L111-L127){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature variance(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The variance equals the mean, so `Var(Y) = phi * V(mu) = mu` since `phi = 1` for Poisson (see `scale_known`). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Variance values $V(\mu) = \mu$, shape `(n,)`. :::
